summary: The set-id rules of a mounted chown in tests/host/fixtures/chown_plan.c, over vfs_chown_plan and its credential helpers extracted from private copies of syscall_fs.c and process.h

argv:
set -e
d=${WORK}/plan
rm -rf "$d"
mkdir -p "$d"
cp rach2/sys/fs/vfs.h rach2/sys/lib/kerrno.h "$d/"
cp ${SRC}/rach2/sys/syscall_fs.c ${SRC}/rach2/sys/proc/process.h "$d/"
sh tests/host/fixtures/chown_plan.sh "$d"
exec ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -g -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -I "$d" tests/host/fixtures/chown_plan.c -o ${WORK}/chown_plan

faults.name: dir
faults.summary: a directory that loses its set-id bits on a change of owner

lines: chown-proof: fail: a directory keeps its set-id bits across a change of owner

faults.name: gexec
faults.summary: setgid cleared on a change of owner whatever group-execute says

lines: chown-proof: fail: setgid stays through a change of owner when group-execute is clear

faults.name: owner
faults.summary: an owner allowed to give a file away

lines: chown-proof: fail: an owner may not give a file away, and the refusal changes nothing

faults.name: group
faults.summary: a change of group judged by the file's group, not the one asked for

lines: chown-proof: fail: an owner may not give a file to a group it is not in

faults.name: userns
faults.summary: root of any user namespace taken as privileged

lines: chown-proof: fail: root of another user namespace may not take a file it does not own
